title: CSS Float
summary: Explains float (left/right) for wrapping text around an element, and clear for stopping later elements from wrapping. The exercise floats images, floats a cat block left and a dog block right, and clears the footer below both. Ends with advice to use floats only for text wrap and to prefer modern layout tools.

concepts.heading: What float does
points: float moves an element to the left or right edge of its container and lets following inline content (text) wrap around it. This mirrors print layout where text flows around a picture.
Values used in practice: left and right. Syntax: img { float: left; }.
In normal flow, an img and each p is block-level and takes a full row. A floated element is lifted out of that flow, so surrounding text wraps around it.
The property goes on the element that floats (the image), but the visible effect appears on the neighbouring text, which wraps.

concepts.heading: Stopping the wrap with clear
points: If a footer follows floated content, it gets pulled up beside the float, which looks wrong; it should sit at the bottom at full width.
The fix is set on the footer, not the float: footer { clear: left | right | both }. It tells the element to drop below earlier floats on that side.
clear: left handles left floats, clear: right handles right floats, clear: both handles a layout that floats elements on both sides.
Typical case: two floated divs (one left, one right) with a footer needing clear: both.

concepts.heading: When to use it
points: Floats used to be stretched into complex page layouts. That is now discouraged because results can be unpredictable.
Use float mainly to wrap text around an image. For layouts, use Flexbox, Grid or frameworks such as Bootstrap (covered later).
(Extra) Floated children do not give their parent any height, a classic reason a container collapses; clear or modern layout avoids this.

task.name: Cats and dogs float layout
task.starting_point: index.html with a div.cat (aquamarine background, h2, img, p) and a div.dog (coral), each at 40% width and display: inline-block, followed by a footer. The two blocks sit side by side and text does not wrap around the images.
task.goal: Match goal.png: text wraps around each image, the cat block hugs the left, the dog block hugs the right, and the footer spans below both.
steps: Add img { float: left; } so each paragraph wraps around its image (needs enough window width).
Add float: left to .cat and float: right to .dog.
The footer jumps up between the blocks; add clear: both to footer so it returns to the bottom.
Slightly different block heights (different text lengths) are expected, not a bug.
task.expected_result: Two coloured columns at the page edges with wrapped text and a full-width footer underneath.

pitfalls: Putting clear on the floated element instead of the one that must drop below.
Footer rising between floated blocks because clear was omitted.
Using float as a general layout system.
(Extra) Repo files include the author footer ('Made with...') which is not part of the exercise.
